method.name: Mann-Kendall trend test on yearly values
method.description: Yearly values: each cell's monthly values are combined into one value per year (mean of its 12 months), keeping only years with all 12 months, so the seasonal cycle does not enter the test. Period tested: 2001-2020. A cell is tested only with at least 16 of 20 complete years (566 cells tested). The trend is the Mann-Kendall test on those yearly values (original Mann-Kendall test (no autocorrelation correction needed); 17% of the tested cells show residual autocorrelation) and its size is Sen's slope (median of the slopes between all pairs of years) times 10, in NDVI units per decade; slopeCi95 is its 95% confidence interval (from the Mann-Kendall variance, Gilbert 1987), also per decade. Because hundreds of cells are tested at once, the p-values are corrected with the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate across all tested cells of this variable; a cell is significant when its adjusted q-value is below 0.05. The pValue shown is the raw p-value of the test, not q. Missing years: the Mann-Kendall test uses only the order of the yearly values, so a missing year does not bias it (it has one value less). Sen's slope uses the real years. Satellite drift check: the Terra overpass time and the yearly NDVI anomaly change in the same years (r = 0.85, 2015-2025). This is a coincidence in time rather than proof of cause (only five years, including the 2023-2024 drought), but to be safe the test stops in 2020. Generated by the SIGNO pipeline (pipeline/), code written with Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code following the team's choices; values come only from the cited NASA and Hansen/UMD datasets.
